title: Publish club-neutral images of the three CourtHive components
description: Implement the configuration approach from WI-142 in the forks and publish versioned images: the tournament server, and the two static front ends (TMX and the public pages) either as small web-server images or as content images mounted by Caddy. Add CI to each fork that builds from the bundle branch (jim-tennis-deploy plus the club-neutral changes, pinned to the upstream base of 2026-09-24, not current upstream), runs that project's existing checks, and publishes to GitHub Container Registry with a version that records the upstream version it is based on. Remove every jim.tennis-specific value from the built output.

recommended_model.name: Opus 5.5
recommended_model.rationale: Build and configuration changes across three TypeScript projects with known past pitfalls.

acceptance_criteria: Three published images, each usable under any hostname without rebuilding
No built file contains jim.tennis, the author's server address, or any secret
Image tags encode the upstream version and the fork revision
Each fork's CI builds and publishes on tag, after its tests pass
The pnpm link-override hazard is handled in CI (build fails clearly if link: entries are present)
Attribution and licence files required by WI-142 are inside each image
Images are built and tested locally under the final names; nothing is pushed to a registry and no publishing tag is pushed until the owner confirms the licence point in the design note
Front-end images contain no source maps
The server image contains src/scripts/admin-user.mjs so the instance service account can be created with upstream's own script

files_to_create: CI workflows and Dockerfiles in each fork
notes: Work happens in three other repositories on their jim-tennis-deploy branches; keep changes minimal so future rebases onto upstream stay cheap, and offer generally useful changes upstream.
Pushing workflow files needs the `workflow` token scope.

See docs/courthive_bundle_design.md (WI-142, 2026-11-22): the club-neutral changes already exist as local commits on branch bundle/club-neutral in the TMX and courthive-public forks (worktrees were in the session scratchpad; the commits are in the fork repositories). Start from them.
See docs/courthive_bundle_design.md (WI-142, 2026-11-22): front ends ship as content images (built files only) copied into a volume by a one-shot service; Caddy stays the stock image.

See docs/courthive_bundle_design.md (WI-142, 2026-11-22): image names ghcr.io/jameshartt/courthive-server, courthive-tmx, courthive-public; tag <upstream version>-jdt.<n>; labels carry the upstream commit and fork commit.
See docs/courthive_bundle_design.md (WI-142, 2026-11-22): each image carries /licenses with the upstream MIT text, a NOTICE naming the fork and upstream commit, and third-party licences.

See docs/courthive_bundle_design.md (WI-142, 2026-11-22): the server image is 1.58 GB because it installs development dependencies (compression is a runtime need listed as a dev dependency); try a production-only install and report the saving.
See docs/courthive_bundle_design.md (WI-142, 2026-11-22): check when TMX requests Google Fonts and record it in docs/outbound_connections.md if it remains.

testing_requirements: Run all three images locally under two hostnames and complete a sign-in and a tournament page load on each

context.user_story: As a club, I want the tournament software as ready-made images so that I never build it.
context.programme: Club-readiness programme (sprints 019-024). Agreed constraints: BHPLTA clubs only; each club self-hosts its own instance; the original author must have no access to any other club's instance (no seeded accounts, no shared or default secrets, no phone-home); passkeys are the default sign-in with passwords as an optional fallback; the captain role is real; SQLite is the only supported database; CourtHive is bundled as an opt-in part of the package so clubs can run their own club championships.
